## 1. New LLM Versions / Major AI Lab Tools
**2026-07-07 — Google expanded Managed Agents in the Gemini API**  
Source: [Google AI Blog](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/developers-tools/expanding-managed-agents-gemini-api/)  
Google announced a Managed Agents expansion for the Gemini API, including background tasks and remote MCP support. The move shifts more agent orchestration into Google’s hosted developer stack.  
**Why it matters:** Google is turning Gemini API from a model endpoint into managed agent infrastructure, reducing developer plumbing while increasing dependence on Google’s runtime.

**2026-07-07 — Anthropic’s Claude Cowork reportedly expanded to web and mobile**  
Source: [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/07/07/the-coding-agent-wars-are-spilling-into-the-rest-of-the-office-claude-cowork/)  
TechCrunch reports Anthropic is expanding Claude Cowork beyond desktop to web and mobile for Max subscribers, with emphasis on background administrative workflows and cross-device task monitoring.  
**Why it matters:** Anthropic is pushing coding-agent patterns into broader office work: persistent tasks, phone monitoring, and review/resume loops.

## 5. Regulation & Policy
**2026-07-07 — Axios reports AI labs weakened some voluntary safety commitments**  
Source: [Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/07/07/report-ai-safety-pledges)  
Axios reports a new Future of Life Institute AI Safety Index finding that several major AI labs weakened or removed prior commitments tied to development pauses at specified risk thresholds. The supplied source is single-source; treat as a governance signal, not a regulatory action.  
**Why it matters:** Voluntary frontier-lab safety commitments remain unstable as a control mechanism, increasing pressure for external standards or enforceable oversight.
